newsitem.title: USA: AT&T cuts U.S. long distance phone rates.
newsitem.headline: AT&T cuts U.S. long distance phone rates.

text.p: AT&T Corp. said Monday it will cut its basic rates for domestic long distance calls by 5 percent during daytime and evening hours and 15 percent during night and weekend hours.

The Basking Ridge, N.J.-based company said the cuts follow a recent Federal Communications Commission order calling for reductions in the access fees long distance companies must pay to local telephone companies.
AT&T said it is passing on all the savings from lower access charges, including a large share for consumers paying basic rates who do not subscribe to optional calling plans.
Under the current basic schedule, a 15-minute coast-to-coast direct-dialed call costs $4.65 during daytime hours, $2.85 during evening hours, and $2.40 during night/weekend hours.
Beginning July 15, the same call will cost $4.35, $2.70 and $1.95, respectively.
The company said the rate reduction will affect AT&T customers who currently are not enrolled in a calling plan.
AT&T's stock fell 25 cents to $35.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
